report: Phase L root-cause diagnostic — GMD duration regression step 25 -> step 50

duration_metric_verification.formula: duration_beats = max(note.end over all tracks) / tpq ; duration_sec = duration_beats * 60 / first_tempo_qpm
duration_metric_verification.tempo_handling: uses score.tempos[0].qpm only (first tempo); no tempo-map changes present in these outputs
duration_metric_verification.consistency_check: pretrained gmd-09 == step-25 gmd-09 exactly (50 notes, 29.0 beats, same tempo 114.52) — metric is stable across models
duration_metric_verification.conclusion: NO metric bug. Duration calculation is consistent and correct; the regression is a real model-behavior change.

per_prompt_gmd_comparison.assessment: PRIMARY regression: notes −87%, duration −45%, velocity range collapsed (min 63→7), pitch range narrowed (44–80 → 30–65)
PRIMARY regression: duration −64% (29.0→10.5) with notes barely changed (50→48); step-25 exactly equals pretrained (suggests regurgitation)

gmd-09.interpretation: Shorter note durations AND compressed time span — the same ~48 notes are packed into ~1/3 the musical time. Rhythmic/temporal compression.

gmd-07.interpretation: Fewer note events, longer sustained notes, compressed time span — rhythmic sparsity / collapse.

training_trajectory.interpretation: Validation loss improves monotonically (lower = better fit) while GMD generation duration regresses. Confirms: lower validation loss does NOT equal better music. Generation quality and validation loss are decoupled.

root_cause.category: Real model-behavior regression (temporal/rhythmic degradation), not a metric artifact or premature termination.
root_cause.mechanism: As training progresses from step 25 to step 50, the model drifts away from pretrained GMD behavior: (1) gmd-09 produces shorter note durations (−59%) and a compressed time span (−68%); (2) gmd-07 produces far fewer note events (−87%) with longer sustains and compressed span (−83%). NRG-CP is unaffected (passes all gates at step 50).
contributing_factors: Source imbalance with equal sampling: NRG-CP has only 275 train examples vs GMD 2062, yet both are sampled at 0.5 probability, so each NRG-CP example is seen ~8x more often than each GMD example — NRG-CP harmonic/chord gradients can interfere with GMD drum/rhythmic patterns.
Model drift: step-50 has moved further from the pretrained weights than step-25, eroding the longer-form rhythmic structure the model needs for sustained drum patterns.
Step-25's pass is fragile: gmd-09 at step-25 equals pretrained exactly (50 notes, 29.0 beats), suggesting partial regurgitation/memorization rather than robust generation.
not_the_cause: Not premature termination: model.generate() emits exactly max_new tokens with eos_count=0 for all generations (verified Phase J).
Not a tokenizer bug: EOS/BOS/PAD decode to silence; tokenizer round-trip note+token counts match on all 8 validation MIDIs (verified Phase J).
Not a duration-calculation bug: metric is tempo-invariant, applied identically, and pretrained==step-25 for gmd-09.

conclusion.step_25_status: Latest verified passing candidate. Passes all gates (NRG-CP and GMD).
conclusion.step_50_status: FAILED — GMD mean duration below gate. Preserved as evidence.
conclusion.steps_75_100: Not evaluated per Phase K stop-at-first-failure rule.
conclusion.next_experiment_justification: Do not simply lower the learning rate or shorten training again without addressing the root cause. The evidence points to source interference between NRG-CP (harmonic/chord, few examples, over-sampled) and GMD (drum/rhythmic, many examples, under-sampled per-example). Next experiment should: (1) rebalance per-example exposure (e.g., proportional sampling or replay), (2) add generation-quality early stopping on held-out generation metrics rather than val loss alone, (3) evaluate per-source (NRG-CP vs GMD) separately, (4) consider GMD-augmented or drum-focused data to strengthen rhythmic patterns before any longer run.
